name: hash-sha256-stream
algorithm: std SHA-256 through the streaming state, fed 1,500-byte pieces (the last piece is the remainder) of splitmix64 bytes, one fresh state per pass, reps passes with a one-byte write-back (mk/hash-sha256-stream.mk).

skip.c: no std hash: C has no standard SHA-256
skip.rust: no std SHA-256: Rust std has none (only SipHash-1-3 in DefaultHasher); no crate stands in

notes: Idiomatic standard library, the streaming case (review finding HMR-3): Mk Sha256State.New/Bytes/Sum, Go crypto/sha256.New, Write per piece, Sum, Zig init/update/final. 1,500 is not a multiple of the block, so the partial-block path of Bytes runs on every piece. Bytes per second = mib * 1048576 * reps / median.
Go: crypto/sha256 uses the SHA extensions (SHA-NI) or AVX2 on amd64 when the CPU has them; Mk is scalar. Zig at -mcpu=x86_64_v2 is scalar.

Checksums: Mk (mk build -release), Zig 0.17.0 (-O ReleaseFast -mcpu=x86_64_v2) and, where it has the function, Go 1.27.3 (GOAMD64=v2 -pgo=off) printed the same quick values on the owner's machine, 2026-11-07 (std-hashmod session 9, HMR-3); the publish-size checksum was agreed by every column in `go run ./tools/bench verify -publish-size`. Not published: no number here is a measurement.
